To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression levels of the oestrogen receptor, IGF1 receptor and IGFBP-3 are correlated with breast cancer risk.

oestradiol upregulates the expression of the IGF receptor in normal breast tissue in vivo, and this may be a mechanism by which oestrogen promotes proliferation in normal breast tissue and thus increases breast cancer risk.

the expression of oestrogen receptor, insulin-like growth factor receptor, and insulin-like growth factor binding protein 3 are all associated with breast cancer, and that the expression of these markers may be useful for predicting risk to breast cancer, and for predicting response to therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new markers of breast cancer risk.

the identification and validation of novel markers of breast cancer risk in the context of metabolic-endocrine pathways, and in particular the insulin-like growth factor (IGF) axis and the oestrogen receptor.
the identification of new risk markers for breast cancer and the development of novel therapies for breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a strong case for a role of the IGF1/IGFBP axis in breast cancer, but that further research is required.
IGF1, ER and GH are involved in breast cancer development and progression, and that their interplay is a complex one.
there is a strong association between breast cancer and IGF1 and that this association may be mediated by the IGF1 receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oestrogens and insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) may be involved in the development of breast carcinoma.

there is a positive correlation between IGF receptor status and ER status and a negative correlation between IGFBP3 and ER status, which may indicate an important interaction between IGF1 and oestrogen signalling in normal and malignant mammary epithelum.
the combined effect oestradiol, IGF1 and IGFR may stimulate proliferation in the breast and increase risk of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGF system is an important regulator of normal mammary epithelial proliferation and differentiation and that it may be a target for the prevention of breast cancer.
the combination of IGF1 with oestradiol may stimulate proliferation in mammary epithelial cells and increase breast cancer.
the IGF1 system is a potential risk marker for the disease, and that this may be mediated by the effects of oestradiols and growth hormone.
